The cheapest Ideogram 4.5 request is not the default. If you omit the quality field on POST https://t.co/rqsJFDzHIW and you are not sending source images, the official API reference says quality defaults to high. On Ideogram's official pricing page, checked Nov 17, 2026 (the page itself is also stamped "as of November 16, 2026"), High is $0.10 per generated image at both 1K and 2K. Low is $0.03. Medium is $0.06.

From Ideogram's API reference, 4.5 model page, pricing page, and API setup guide:

Ideogram 4.5 Generate - POST /v2/image/generate/ideogram-4-5
- Prompt only, no source images:
- Very Low: not available
- Low: $0.03
- Medium: $0.06
- High: $0.10, and this is the documented default
- With source images (up to 5, first image is the one being edited, the rest are references):
- Very Low: $0.008. Official note: very_low requires source images
- Low: $0.03
- Medium: $0.06, and this is the documented default when source images are present
- High: $0.22
- Official model page: each image has a fixed price. It does not change with prompt length, the number of reference images, or the output resolution
- The generate reference still tiers billing labels by resolved pixels: up to 1024x1024 bills as 1K, above that as 2K, and an auto size bills as 2K. On today's pricing table, the 1K and 2K rows are the same dollar amount. Do not assume that will stay true. Bill against the live table
- Without source images, size omitted or auto picks a supported size from the prompt. With source images, auto is the default and picks a supported 2K size
- magic_prompt defaults to auto, which rewrites and expands a natural-language prompt before generation. Set off if you want to keep your wording. Official note: off still converts the text into a structured prompt. A valid structured JSON prompt skips magic prompt unless magic_prompt is on
- async defaults to false, so the request waits for the images. Set async or supply webhook_url to get a generation_id and poll GET /v2/generations/{generation_id}. Webhook deliveries are signed with Ed25519 and can be verified against https://t.co/WdIgZBZuhU
- dry_run is a query parameter and defaults to false. Set dry_run=true to validate and price the exact request without generating, storing, billing, or running a safety review. The response is a PriceQuote
- If an image fails safety checks, is_image_safe is false and url is empty. A prompt that fails safety checks returns 422
- Official setup page: image and video links created by the Ideogram API expire. Download what you want to keep. The page does not publish an exact lifetime, so do not invent one

Ideogram 4.5 Precise Edit - POST /v2/image/precise-edit/ideogram-4-5
- Very Low: $0.008
- Low: $0.03
- Medium: $0.06
- High: $0.22

Prepaid API balance, from the official setup guide: requests draw down a credit balance at the published API price. You can add $10, $20, $50, $100, or a custom amount between $1 and $300. The balance cannot exceed $300. Auto recharge starts off. If you turn it on, the documented defaults are a $10 threshold and a $20 top-up. If you also have an Ideogram subscription, API requests use its monthly credits first when they cover the whole request, and the API balance otherwise. Auth is the Api-Key header. With no payment method or credits, requests are rejected with 402. The official pricing page states a default rate limit of 10 in-flight requests. Payment obligations are non-cancellable, and fees paid are non-refundable.

A 1,000-image text-to-image batch at the default High quality is $100. The same count at Low is $30, and at Medium it is $60. That gap only helps if Low or Medium is actually good enough for the job. If you attach source images and leave quality at High, the same 1,000 images are $220, not $100. Quote the request with dry_run first.

If you want one key, async jobs (webhook or polling), and prepaid credits in front of several image models, https://t.co/dzB8b0BSY3 is built for that shape. It does not change Ideogram's default quality, and it does not keep an Ideogram result URL alive past the vendor's own limit.

note_tweet.text:
"OpenAI Agents SDK: Making Multi-Agent Workflow into a Light Skeleton"

What this SDK wants to solve is not to "write another layer of arrangement framework that binds all models to death", but to extract those common components in multi-agent cooperation and make a set of detachable and replaceable Python skeletons.

It puts several things into the same set of primitives: Agent with instructions, tools, guards and handover; Sandbox Agent pre-configures containers to carry long-time tasks; Realtime Agent takes WebSocket to make low-delay speech and multimodal; Voice Pipeline strings speech to text, agent process and text to speech into a stream. Standing behind it are Python SDK, Requests, MCP and Python SDK, as well as options such as LiteLLM and any-llm, which can support 100+ models other than OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions. The foreground is written in pure Python, and synchronous, asynchronous and Jupyter can run.

What is more interesting is that it extends "calling" to "governance": the agent can be used as a tool or as a whole; The guards check the input and output, remember the history of the session, track and spread each run, and people can be invited back halfway.

The boundary is also unambiguous. The PR of the warehouse is only open to collaborators, and only issue can be mentioned externally. It delivers the application of the skeleton instead of the finished product. The container sandbox has to borrow Docker client or hosting scheme on Windows.

For those who want to use multi-agent from "a running demo" to "an assembly line that can be checked, controlled and changed", this SDK does provide a very light landing path: first, break the collaboration into roles, and then string the roles into processes.

Source: github | "OpenAI/OpenAI-Agents-Python"
